why: Compliment = to praise; complement = to complete or blend well with, so only C pairs both correctly.
Deify = to make a god of someone; defy = to oppose or resist.
Stationery (with -e-) = writing and office material; stationary (with -a-) = immobile.
Complaisant = eager to please; complacent = smugly self-satisfied or over-confident.
In British usage enquiry = a general request for information while inquiry = a formal investigation.
Masterful = imperious or domineering; masterly = highly skilful, so D alone gets both.
Boarder = a person who receives food and lodging; border = a boundary.
Concurrent = occurring at the same time; consecutive = occurring one after the other, which A states exactly while C hedges consecutive as 'thereafter'.
An epitaph is the words written on a tombstone (not the stone itself, as A says) and an epithet is a phrase expressing an attribute.
Discomfort = unease; discomfit = to embarrass or disconcert.
Rhetoric-1 and jargon-3 are fixed, leaving vernacular-4 (a particular group's language) and parlance-2 ('common parlance'), which only D satisfies.
Truth is internecine-3, revoke-1, exonerate-2, venerable-4 and NO option matches; D is best as the only one with internecine-3 and revoke-1, though it swaps exonerate and venerable.
Atonement-4 (making amends), sacrilege-2, clawback-1 (retrieving money paid), bandwagon-3.
Felony-3 (serious crime), restitution-2, chagrin-4 (distress from humiliation), diatribe-1 (long written criticism).
Truth is wrangle-3, wacky-2, codex-4, postscript-1 and no option offers wrangle-3; C is best, correct on wacky-2 and postscript-1 with only the 3/4 pair transposed.
Inveterate-1 (habitual), sangfroid-3 (calm under pressure), oracy-2 (speech ability), interment-4 (burial).
Truth is ex gratia-2, suo moto-3, arraignment-4, locus standi-1 and no option offers ex gratia-2; A is best, correct on arraignment-4 and locus standi-1 with ex gratia and suo moto transposed.
Fait accompli-1, hedonism-4 (pleasure), hoplarchy-2 (rule by the military), ochlocracy-3 (rule by the mob).
Nadir-3 (lowest point), rhapsody-4 (effusive praise), amble-1 (walk slowly), pittance-2 (tiny sum).
Damp squib-3 (disappointing), excerpt-4 (short extract), rostrum-1 (raised platform), scourge-2 (cause of great trouble).
An iconoclast attacks or rejects accepted beliefs and traditions, not merely a single cultural icon.
An axiom is a principle accepted as self-evidently true, not a rule of conduct or a statement of equality.
Holistic means treating the whole system rather than its individual parts; D is a 'holy' sound-alike trap.
Obsequious = fawning, excessively eager to please or obey a superior.
A pachyderm is a thick-skinned mammal such as an elephant; D is a spelling trap on 'patchy'.
Ubiquitous = present everywhere, i.e. wide presence; the other three all denote restricted presence.
Desiccate = to dry out thoroughly; C is the only drying option, the others being cutting or salt-removal.
Deleterious = harmful; A, B and D are traps on the sound-alike 'delete'.
Equivocate = to use deliberately vague or ambiguous language to conceal the truth; the 'equi-' options are sound-alike traps.
Indolent = habitually lazy or averse to exertion.
